To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have implemented the Homotopic Path Method (HPP), which is a deterministic method, in an FPGA and have developed an automatic algorithm for the repulsion parameter of the HPP, which is the first of its kind.

the proposed method is a complete deterministic collision-free path planning scheme for low degrees of freedom, which is implemented for the first time in a low-cost FPGA and it exhibits path calculation times 5 to 100 times better than other path finding methods.
the FPGA implementation of the HPPM path finding algorithm is the fastest and most efficient one.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a complete path planning method, implemented in a reprogrammable device, which allows us a real-time control of autonomous mobile robots.
the design, implementation and testing of a complete path finding algorithm, which is based on a deterministic approach.

the design and implementation of a complete deterministic path planning scheme, with automatic assignment of the repulsion parameters and with dead end and risk trajectory detection, which is able to calculate collision free paths with the minimum number of obstacles crossed.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed method is more efficient than the others in terms of computational resources consumption.

the HPPM with automatic assignment of repulsion parameter is a very efficient and robust path planning algorithm for low DoF robots, which is also easy to implement and can be executed on a low-cost hardware platform such as FPGA, which makes it very attractive for the development of autonomous robots.
the FPGA implementation is 5 to 100 times more efficient than the PC implementation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed method can be implemented in low DoF robots with a very low memory consumption, allowing them to be more autonomous, and therefore more useful.

our proposal is the first implementation of the HPPM on FPGA, which is also the first implementation of an automatic assignment algorithm of the repulsive parameter, and the first implementation of a dead end route and collision risk trajectories algorithm.

the proposed HPPM method with the automatic repulsion parameter assignment and the dead end route discrimination algorithms is a fast, efficient, reliable, and deterministic method for path planning in low DoF environments.

the proposed method is suitable to be implemented in low power and low cost devices like FPGAs, which can be used for real time applications in autonomous robotics.
